end.summary:
Practised the relation between consecutive odd-number sums and square numbers.
Saanvi correctly identified 1 + 3 = 4 and explained 4 as 2².
They used dot layers and L-shape ideas to describe adding odd numbers.
They gave three unaided correct attempts for the target skill.
Teach-back was not passed; confusion about the 3-dot L-shape was expressed during the lesson.
end.parentNote: Asha practised building square numbers by adding consecutive odd numbers, using number sentences and dot layers. Saanvi correctly connected 1 + 3 to 4 and later used the square-number pattern for answers such as 25 and 225. They mixed up how a 3-dot L-shape fits around a 2×2 square; this was not clearly corrected by the end. At home, draw a 1×1 square, then add an L-shaped layer of 3, 5, and 7 dots to make 2×2, 3×3, and 4×4 squares.
